sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.text_preview: D IGITAL-TO-ANALOG (D/A) converters are essential components of modern applications such as video signal processing, digital signal synthesis, and both wired and wireless transmitters. Formerly, time-domain applications such as high-resolution displays and video signal processing were the main drivers of high-speed D/A development [1], [2]. sections.text_preview: The converter architecture is shown in Fig. 1. sections.text_preview: The primary specification for the converter is SFDR. As both static and dynamic performance contribute to SFDR, the error sources which affect both must be considered. sections.text_preview: For each extra segmented bit, the number of switching latches doubles. sections.text_preview: The goal of the design was to reduce random and systematic mismatch errors through good layout placement and routing.
